Extended-tick rerun of Exp-001 full-governance baseline. Identical in all parameters except ticks: 2000 vs. 500. Tests whether epistemic_accuracy, which was identical between Exp-000 (null, 0.6) and Exp-001 (full governance, 0.6) at 500 ticks, diverges over longer timescales. The non-divergence is either a timescale effect (full governance needs more than 500 ticks to improve accuracy above chance) or a metric pathology (accuracy is not responding to governance primitives). This experiment distinguishes the two. Baseline is Exp-001 (seed 42, 500 ticks, small_world, all primitives enabled).

Confidence ablation against full-governance baseline. Identical to Exp-001 except confidence primitive is disabled. Tests whether the reversion-rate and resolution-rate contrast between Exp-000 (null) and Exp-001 (full governance) is attributable to Confidence specifically, or to Reversibility, or to both jointly. Separates the Confidence effect from the Reversibility effect on total_reversions and contested_claim_resolution_rate. Baseline is Exp-001 (seed 42, 500 ticks, small_world).

Extended-tick rerun of Exp-001 full-governance baseline. Identical in all parameters except ticks: 2000 vs. 500. Tests whether epistemic_accuracy, which was identical between Exp-000 (null, 0.6) and Exp-001 (full governance, 0.6) at 500 ticks, diverges over longer timescales. The non-divergence is either a timescale effect (full governance needs more than 500 ticks to improve accuracy above chance) or a metric pathology (accuracy is not responding to governance primitives). This experiment distinguishes the two. Baseline is Exp-001 (seed 42, 500 ticks, small_world, all primitives enabled).

Confidence ablation against full-governance baseline. Identical to Exp-001 except confidence primitive is disabled. Tests whether the reversion-rate and resolution-rate contrast between Exp-000 (null) and Exp-001 (full governance) is attributable to Confidence specifically, or to Reversibility, or to both jointly. Separates the Confidence effect from the Reversibility effect on total_reversions and contested_claim_resolution_rate. Baseline is Exp-001 (seed 42, 500 ticks, small_world).
